ground_truth_root_cause: Redis primary node redis-primary-01 ran out of memory (OOM) due to a rogue client (client_conn_00089 from 10.44.12.55) that left a MONITOR session running since 01:51:09 UTC. Redis MONITOR streams every command processed by the server to the subscribed client; at the observed traffic volume this produced approximately 180 GB/hr of output buffered in the client output buffer. Because the client output buffer limit was set to 0 (unlimited), Redis allocated unbounded heap until used_memory hit the 30 GB maxmemory ceiling. With eviction policy=noeviction, all subsequent write commands were rejected with OOM errors, rendering checkout-service unable to persist session or order state and causing a full service outage. This MONITOR session predates all recent deploys and is unrelated to the payment-service idempotency key changes.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately kill the MONITOR client: connect to Redis via redis-cli and run CLIENT KILL ID 00089 or CLIENT KILL ADDR 10.44.12.55. If Redis is unresponsive to management commands, force-restart the Redis primary so the replica is promoted or the primary recovers after restart. 2. After restart, verify memory reclamation via INFO memory and confirm used_memory drops below maxmemory. 3. Set client output buffer limits in redis.conf: client-output-buffer-limit normal 256mb 64mb 60 to prevent recurrence. 4. Identify and remediate the process on 10.44.12.55 that initiated the MONITOR session, likely a debug script left running unattended. 5. Add a monitoring alert for any connected client running MONITOR to detect future occurrences within seconds.
red_herring: The payment-service deploy (SHA e23b71dc40f8a16, deployed at 01:10 UTC, approximately 54 minutes before the incident) is highly suspicious: it modifies the Stripe charge client, introduces new retry logic, and alters transaction logging, all in the critical payment flow that checkout-service depends on. A follow-up checkout-service deploy (SHA f45d08c93e2b174) was pushed only 28 minutes before the incident to surface the new idempotency key, and a third deploy (SHA 07a1e6b52f9cd30) landed just 11 minutes before the outage. Together these form a cluster of payment-flow changes immediately preceding the failure. However, the logs contain multiple pieces of exculpatory evidence: (a) payment-service logs at 02:04:26 and 02:04:27 explicitly confirm the idempotency layer is functioning correctly with no payment errors detected; (b) Stripe charges succeed normally at 02:03:11 through 02:03:15, well after all deploys, with zero payment-layer errors anywhere in the log window; (c) the Redis degradation is definitively attributed to a MONITOR client (client_conn_00089) connected since 01:51:09 UTC, which is 19 minutes before the incident and predates no deploy activity; (d) redis-proxy explicitly logs that the single MONITOR client is producing approximately 180 GB/hr of output buffer accumulation with client output buffer reaching 28.1 GB against an unlimited limit; (e) Redis OOM errors affect all write paths uniformly including sessions, carts, and orders, which is inconsistent with a retry storm from the payment path and entirely consistent with a memory ceiling being hit due to output buffer exhaustion.
